categories.name: AI Assistants
categories.tagline: Interface surfaces for products built on LLMs.
categories.description: Composed sections for AI products — conversation threads with streaming and markdown, prompt composers with attachments and model selection, reasoning traces, agent tool timelines, and citation displays. Each block renders standalone with realistic data and shares one message contract, so they compose into a working chat surface.

categories.name: Pricing
categories.tagline: Sections that ask for money and get an answer.
categories.description: Seven complete pricing sections, each a different art direction: staggered serif panels on a dot grid, pastel gradient cards, a dark comparison matrix, a Swiss-style table with crop marks, cream serif cards with a glowing featured plan, a brutalist banner table, and plans printed as thermal receipts. Every block ships with realistic plan data, its own palette themed for light and dark, live billing interactions, and scroll-triggered entrances.

categories.name: Tables
categories.tagline: The tables real products run on, ready to copy.
categories.description: Fifteen data table sections covering the screens a SaaS product actually ships — payments, team members, invoices, orders, customers, API keys, audit logs, deployments, feature flags, support tickets, analytics, a market watchlist, inventory, a leaderboard, and a file browser. Every one is built on the same typed Data Table engine, so sorting glides rows into place, selection raises a bulk-action bar, and reduced motion is respected — while each block brings its own columns, Iconly glyphs, people avatars and status colors.

categories.name: Charts
categories.tagline: Every chart, live, with the source beside it.
categories.description: The Spectrum chart library, rendered as blocks. A dependency-free SVG market family — candlesticks with a volume pane, an order book ladder, market depth, RSI and MACD indicators and portfolio drawdown against cost basis; area, bar, line, composed, pie, radar and radial charts on Recharts; a latency histogram with percentile pins; and the dashboard set — KPI stat cards, a cohort retention grid and a year of daily activity. Every chart renders live at full size with its variants on pills, a copyable source file, and the loading, empty and error states it ships with.

categories.name: Footers
categories.tagline: Page-width footers that do something when you touch them.
categories.description: Twenty-five interactive footer sections for enterprise platforms, AI products and small teams — mega sitemaps with region and language selectors, trust rows with SOC 2 and ISO scope, live service status with uptime sparklines, model availability grids, terminal and ask-the-docs inputs, oversized wordmarks, marquees, newsletter and waitlist capture. Every glyph is an inlined Iconly Pro Bold path, so a block copies out with no icon dependency, and every entrance, hover and state change is CSS — the links render even if JavaScript never arrives.

blocks.name: Loading State
blocks.description: A pixel-grid loader with a shimmering label and live elapsed timer.
blocks.summary: What fills the gap before the first token. A nine-cell pixel grid animates a chevron wavefront or an orbiting comet, next to a shimmering label and an elapsed timer in mono tabular figures.
hardParts: A timer that ticks every 100ms needs tabular figures or the layout wobbles on every frame
The 650ms cycle is shorter than the sweep so two wavefronts are always in flight
Reduced motion freezes the grid to its dim state while the timer keeps ticking
blocks.aiHints: Render while a long-running AI task has produced no output yet. Purely visual; label and variant are props. Self-contained — its keyframes ship inside the component.

blocks.name: Reasoning Trace
blocks.description: An expandable chain-of-thought trace with a live thinking timer.
blocks.summary: Shows the model's reasoning before its answer. Streams step by step while thinking, tracks elapsed time, and collapses to a one-line summary when done.
hardParts: Animating the height of streaming content — height:auto is unanimatable and max-height guesses wrong
Collapsing must not jump the scroll position of the thread above
An elapsed timer needs tabular numbers or the label wobbles every tick
blocks.aiHints: Render above an assistant message to expose reasoning. Accepts steps plus a status of thinking or complete. Presentational only.

blocks.name: Streaming Text
blocks.description: A streamed answer with inline citations, sources, and follow-ups.
blocks.summary: A single streamed answer outside a full thread — token-by-token text with inline citation markers, a compact source row or expanded source list, and follow-up prompts that stagger in when the answer settles.
hardParts: Word-chunked streaming reads as inference; per-character reads as a typewriter
Citation markers arrive in the stream before their sources render
Follow-ups must not shift layout while text is still arriving
blocks.aiHints: Render a single streamed answer outside a full thread. Accepts text, citations and follow-up prompts; streaming drives the caret.

blocks.name: Prompt Composer
blocks.description: A prompt input with attachments, a model picker, and a stop state.
blocks.summary: The input surface of an AI product: an autosizing textarea with attachment chips, a model picker that opens upward, a character budget, and a send control that becomes stop while a response streams.
hardParts: Autosize with a max height that then scrolls, without per-keystroke jitter
The model menu opens upward so it never collides with a thread above
Swapping send for stop without the button changing size
blocks.aiHints: Use as the input of an AI product. Emits onSend with text and model id; set isGenerating to swap send for stop. Enter is IME-safe.

blocks.name: Chat Empty State
blocks.description: A first-run greeting with staggered suggestion chips.
blocks.summary: The first thing every user sees. A greeting, an honest subtitle, and suggestion chips that stagger in and feed the composer.
hardParts: Least technically hard, highest product leverage — it is the first impression
Stagger must be capped or a long chip list turns into a wait
Chips must feed the composer without a page of wiring
blocks.aiHints: Render instead of the thread when there are no messages. Emits onSelectPrompt so a chip can populate the composer.

blocks.name: Message Actions
blocks.description: Per-message controls — copy, regenerate, and thumb feedback.
blocks.summary: The action row on an assistant message: copy with a blur-crossfade check, regenerate with a half-turn, and thumb feedback that fills and pops. Hover-revealed on pointer devices, keyboard-reachable, always visible on touch.
hardParts: Hover-reveal that is also keyboard-reachable and always visible on touch — three access models, one component
Copy must yield source markdown, not rendered DOM text
Feedback state must survive being toggled off
blocks.aiHints: Attach below an assistant message inside a group/message container. Hover-revealed on pointer devices, always visible on touch.

blocks.name: Citation Sources
blocks.description: Inline citation markers with hover previews or a footnote list.
blocks.summary: Grounds an answer in its sources. Numbered markers sit inline in the text and reveal a hovercard on hover or focus; the footnote variant lists every source with domain and snippet.
hardParts: Numbering must stay stable when sources deduplicate by domain
A hovercard that works on focus as well as hover
Markers must not break line height or text rhythm
blocks.aiHints: Wrap answer text containing [n] markers. Accepts Citation[] indexed from 1; hovercards need no JS positioning.

blocks.name: Agent Steps
blocks.description: A timeline of tool calls with status, arguments, results, and parallel sub-steps.
blocks.summary: Visualises what an agent actually did: each tool call with its status, arguments, duration and result, including parallel sub-steps rendered side by side.
hardParts: A real state machine — pending, running, success, error — not a spinner
Arguments stay readable without blowing the layout: truncate, never wrap
Parallel calls need a visibly different treatment from sequential ones
blocks.aiHints: Render inside an assistant message to show tool use. Accepts ToolCall[] with nested children; expandable results use no height hacks.

blocks.name: Tool Chips
blocks.description: Compact tool-call chips that expand into their arguments and result.
blocks.summary: Tool calls as a row or stack of compact chips — status dot, mono name, duration — with one shared panel that expands to show the selected call's arguments and result.
hardParts: One expanded panel shared across chips keeps the layout calm
Status must be legible from a 6px dot alone
Chips wrap without orphaning their durations
blocks.aiHints: A denser alternative to agent-steps for inline tool use. Accepts ToolCall[]; one chip expands at a time.

blocks.name: Approval Card
blocks.description: A human-in-the-loop approval for an action an agent wants to take.
blocks.summary: An agent proposes; a human decides. The card states the action and its consequence, and the decision crossfades in place with an audit line preserved.
hardParts: Show the consequence clearly enough to decide on
The decided state must preserve an audit trail
Approve and dismiss must not be visual equals
blocks.aiHints: Render when an agent proposes an irreversible action. Emits onDecide; the decided state crossfades in place.

blocks.name: Model Selector
blocks.description: A model picker as a radio list or segmented control, with badges and disabled states.
blocks.summary: Model choice as a radio list with descriptions, badges and disabled states, or as a segmented control whose active pill slides between options.
hardParts: Disabled options must stay visible — capability differences are information
The sliding pill needs transform, not layout animation
Radio semantics without a form library
blocks.aiHints: Accepts ModelOption[]; controlled or uncontrolled. Disabled options stay visible so capability differences are legible.

blocks.name: Usage Meter
blocks.description: A context-window meter with token counts and estimated cost.
blocks.summary: Context-window state at a glance: a meter that turns amber past 75 percent and red past 90, token counts in tabular figures, and an estimated cost.
hardParts: Tabular numerals or every tick shifts the layout
Threshold colors must be meaningful, not decorative
The bar animates width smoothly without repaint jank
blocks.aiHints: Accepts a UsageState. Threshold colors at 75 and 90 percent; numerals are tabular so the layout never wobbles.

blocks.name: Voice Input
blocks.description: A voice recorder pill with animated level bars and a live timer.
blocks.summary: A recorder pill that moves through idle, recording and processing. Level bars animate on staggered offsets, the timer ticks in mono, and cancel or confirm sit a thumb-width apart.
hardParts: Level bars from staggered CSS offsets, no audio API needed for the preview
Three permission-adjacent states with distinct affordances
Reduced motion needs a static-but-alive treatment
blocks.aiHints: Controlled or uncontrolled recording states: idle, recording, processing. Reduced motion freezes the bars; the timer still ticks.

blocks.name: Inline Edit
blocks.description: A selection-anchored AI edit: suggestion toolbar, word diff, accept or reject.
blocks.summary: AI editing anchored to a selection: the highlighted span grows a floating action, the suggestion arrives as a word-level diff, and accepting swaps the text in place.
hardParts: A floating action anchored to an inline selection across line wraps
Word-level diff that reads at a glance — del and ins, not walls of red and green
Accepting must swap text without the paragraph jumping
blocks.aiHints: Render over editable prose. Shows the selection, a floating action, then a del/ins diff; accepting swaps the text in place.

blocks.name: Thinking Dots
blocks.description: A minimal typing indicator — bouncing dots or a sliding bar.
blocks.summary: The lightest possible signal that the assistant is alive. Three dots bounce on staggered offsets, or a bar slides its track, next to a quiet label.
hardParts: Stagger offsets must be irregular enough not to read as a metronome
role=status announces once, not per bounce
Reduced motion freezes to the dim state
blocks.aiHints: Render while the assistant is preparing a reply and no richer state applies. Purely visual; label is a prop.

blocks.name: Task Rows
blocks.description: Live agent task rows with status badges and expandable notes.
blocks.summary: What a background agent is doing right now: each row carries a status icon, a mono detail, a status badge, and an expandable note for the rows that finished.
hardParts: Four statuses with distinct affordances, legible without color
A spinning icon that does not blur at small sizes
Expanding one row must not shift its neighbours
blocks.aiHints: Render a background agent's work queue. Accepts TaskRow[] with queued, running, completed and failed statuses; rows with notes expand.

blocks.name: Agent Plan
blocks.description: An editable plan checklist the agent proposes before running.
blocks.summary: The agent proposes, the human prunes. Numbered steps with checkboxes, struck through when excluded, and a run button that counts what survives.
hardParts: Excluded steps stay visible — an edited plan is still a plan
Checkbox semantics without a form library
The run button must reflect the live enabled count
blocks.aiHints: Render before executing a multi-step plan. Steps toggle on and off; onRun receives the enabled step ids.

blocks.name: Web Search
blocks.description: Agent search results with a live reading indicator.
blocks.summary: What the agent is reading and in what order: the query in mono, results with favicon dots and snippets, and a reading badge that walks down the list.
hardParts: The reading state must draw the eye without flashing
Idle results dim rather than disappear
Snippets clamp to one line so the list stays scannable
blocks.aiHints: Render while an agent searches the web. Accepts results with reading, read and idle states; the query renders in mono.

blocks.name: Diff View
blocks.description: Proposed file changes with per-file accept and reject.
blocks.summary: Changes an agent wants to make, shown as unified diffs with add and remove lines, per-file +/− counts, and accept or reject controls that record the decision in place.
hardParts: Rejected files dim but stay — an audit trail, not a deletion
Diff lines never wrap; horizontal scroll preserves alignment
Accept and reject must not be visual equals
blocks.aiHints: Render changes an agent proposes to files. Accepts FileDiff[]; accept and reject decide per file and the decision is recorded in place.

blocks.name: Code Block
blocks.description: An AI code block with a file header, copy, and line collapse.
blocks.summary: Code as an assistant emits it: a file header, optional line numbers, a copy control with the blur-crossfade check, and a collapse that keeps long output honest.
hardParts: Copy must take the full source even while collapsed
Line numbers are tabular and unselectable
The expander states exactly how many lines it hides
blocks.aiHints: Render code inside an assistant reply. Collapses past collapsedLines with an expander; copy takes the full source either way.

blocks.name: Insight Cards
blocks.description: Metric cards with spark bars, trend deltas, and an AI note.
blocks.summary: Metrics with a voice: the number in mono, a trend delta with its arrow, spark bars with the latest period emphasised, and one line of AI annotation under a hairline.
hardParts: Spark bars emphasise the latest period, not the tallest
Deltas are signed, colored and tabular
The AI note must read as annotation, not as another metric
blocks.aiHints: Render AI-computed metrics. Accepts insights with a value, a signed change, spark points and an optional annotation line.

blocks.name: Error State
blocks.description: A failed-generation state with a preserved prompt and retry.
blocks.summary: Failure without drama: what went wrong, the reassurance that the prompt survived, and a retry that spins while it works.
hardParts: The message must say the prompt is preserved — that is the actual fear
Retry disables while retrying or users double-fire
The inline variant must fit a thread row
blocks.aiHints: Render when generation fails. The retry control shows a spinner while retrying; the inline variant fits inside a thread.

blocks.name: Quota Banner
blocks.description: A message-quota banner with a live reset countdown.
blocks.summary: The cap, stated plainly: messages left, a meter that turns amber at the limit, a live mm:ss reset countdown in tabular mono, and the upgrade path.
hardParts: A live countdown needs tabular figures or it jitters every second
Amber at exhaustion; red is for errors, not billing
The compact pill must fit a composer footer
blocks.aiHints: Render when a usage cap approaches or hits. Accepts used, limit and resetsInSeconds; the countdown ticks live.

blocks.name: Memory Chips
blocks.description: What the assistant remembers, as removable chips.
blocks.summary: Assistant memory made legible: each remembered fact is a chip with a remove control, plus a dashed chip to add more. Forgetting something is one click.
hardParts: Forgetting must be one click, never a menu
Chips stagger in but removal is instant
The empty state explains where memories come from
blocks.aiHints: Render saved assistant memory. Chips remove with an X and stagger in; onAdd renders a dashed add chip.

blocks.name: Suggestion Banner
blocks.description: An inline AI suggestion with apply and dismiss.
blocks.summary: A proactive nudge with manners: the suggestion and its reasoning, a quiet dismiss, and an apply that collapses the banner into a confirmation pill.
hardParts: Applied state collapses to a pill instead of lingering
Dismiss must be quieter than apply
The reasoning line earns the interruption
blocks.aiHints: Render a proactive suggestion. Apply collapses it to a confirmation pill; dismiss removes it. Controlled or uncontrolled.

blocks.name: Status Tracker
blocks.description: A staged progress tracker for long-running AI jobs.
blocks.summary: Long jobs in stages: completed stages check off, the active stage pulses while its connector fills, and the minimal variant compresses it all into one bar.
hardParts: Progress lives in the connectors, not just the dots
Stage labels stay legible at 9.5px mono or they are noise
The minimal variant must collapse to a single honest percentage
blocks.aiHints: Render multi-stage jobs like ingestion or fine-tuning. Accepts stages, an activeIndex and 0–1 progress within the active stage.

blocks.name: Conversation List
blocks.description: A date-grouped conversation sidebar with pinning.
blocks.summary: Chat history that stays organised: date-grouped rows, an active state, and a pin that reveals on hover, stays put on touch, and holds favourites at hand.
hardParts: The pin is hover-revealed on pointer devices but always present on touch
Date grouping happens in data, not in the component's opinion of time
Active and pinned are independent states
blocks.aiHints: Render chat history. Conversations group by date labels; rows select, and a hover-revealed pin keeps favourites.

blocks.name: Offset Tiers
blocks.description: Staggered serif panels on a dot grid, with one entry price and expert CTAs.
blocks.summary: Three square-cornered panels step down the page over a dot-grid canvas, each split by hairlines into name, features, and a footer. Serif display names, blue circular checks, and a single "From" price on the first tier — the other two send you to a person.
hardParts: Staggered offsets must collapse to a flat stack on mobile without leaving dead space
The dot grid has to live behind the panels, not inside them, or it reads as texture on the cards
Only one tier carries a price, so the footers need equal weight without pretending parity
blocks.aiHints: A consultative, sales-led pricing section for services and high-touch products. Takes Plan[]; a null price renders "Talk to us to find out more". Carries its own canvas and themes for light and dark. Optional eyebrow, heading, and subheading props render a headline styled in this block’s own art direction.

blocks.name: Gradient Tiers
blocks.description: Pastel gradient card headers with icons and color-coded inheritance labels.
blocks.summary: Three columns in one hairline frame, each washed from the top with its own pastel — blue, chartreuse, violet — under a matching icon. Serif names, a price row that pairs the figure with its qualifier, and "Everything in X, plus:" labels tinted per column.
hardParts: The gradient wash has to fade out before the checklist or every row fights a tint
Per-column accent colors must agree across icon, label, and badge without a token system
The price row baseline-aligns a figure and a right-hand note that wrap independently
blocks.aiHints: A warm editorial pricing section for API and credit-based products. Prices come as display strings via the notes prop, so "Free", "$250 /mo" and "Custom pricing" all render alike. Themes for light and dark — the pastel washes become deep tints on dark. Optional eyebrow, heading, and subheading props render a headline styled in this block’s own art direction.

blocks.name: Dark Matrix
blocks.description: A dark comparison table with dashed rows, mint checks, and per-plan CTA pills.
blocks.summary: A dark comparison table. Plan headers carry an icon, a name, and a pill CTA; group labels break the grid into sections; data rows sit on a slightly lighter panel behind dashed rules, with mint checks, muted crosses, and hint circles on ambiguous labels.
hardParts: Row strips need a bg one step above the canvas or the dashed rules read as clutter
Mixing dashed row rules with solid column rules means styling borders per edge, not per element
Hint circles must expose their text to screen readers, not just to hover
blocks.aiHints: The long comparison table for a dark pricing page. Takes plans plus FeatureGroup[] with positional values; hints map row labels to tooltip text. Themes light and dark; scrolls horizontally under 720px. Optional eyebrow, heading, and subheading props render a headline styled in this block’s own art direction.

blocks.name: Blueprint Tiers
blocks.description: A Swiss-style pricing table with crop marks, mono labels, and a royal-blue accent.
blocks.summary: Pricing drawn like a technical sheet: columns divided by hairlines with registration marks at the intersections, mono uppercase chips, per-column billed-yearly switches, and a diagonal hatch band closing the section. The featured CTA is royal blue inside corner ticks.
hardParts: Crop marks sit on grid intersections, so they must be positioned off the borders, not the content
Each paid column owns its own yearly toggle - one shared switch would misprice the others
The hatch band is a repeating gradient, not an image, so it must align to the hairline grid
blocks.aiHints: A technical, engineering-flavored pricing section including its own centered header (eyebrow, heading, subheading props). Per-plan yearly toggles switch between monthly and annual prices. Themes for light and dark.

blocks.name: Serif Tiers
blocks.description: Cream serif cards with a black featured card lit by a crimson glow.
blocks.summary: Warm and editorial: serif names and serif prices on soft cream cards, star-glyph feature bullets, and a centered Monthly/Yearly pill. The featured plan turns black and glows crimson from its lower corner under a rose-gradient POPULAR pill.
hardParts: The glow is two stacked blurred circles, and clipping them needs overflow-hidden without cutting the card shadow
Serif digits are not tabular, so the rolling price needs per-digit width control to avoid wobble
White pill CTAs must read as buttons on cream and on black with the same treatment
blocks.aiHints: A warm, consumer-friendly pricing section including its own centered header. The billing toggle rolls per-user prices. Cream in light, warm charcoal in dark; the featured card stays black with its ember in both.

blocks.name: Banner Tiers
blocks.description: A brutalist plan table whose featured column wears a blue banner on top.
blocks.summary: A display-serif headline over three bordered columns fused into one table, with mono CTAs and circled blue checks on hairline feature rows. The featured column is outlined in royal blue and carries a solid blue "Most popular" banner above its header; a rectangular blue switch flips yearly and monthly.
hardParts: The banner extends above the grid, so the section needs reserved headroom or it clips
Adjacent column borders double to 2px unless each seam is owned by exactly one column
Feature rows align across columns only if every cell is one line - the copy is part of the layout
blocks.aiHints: A bold, developer-tool pricing section including its own centered serif header. The switch swaps yearly and monthly prices. Themes for light and dark with a #2337f0 accent.

blocks.name: Receipt Tiers
blocks.description: Plans printed as thermal receipts with torn edges, dotted leaders, and a rubber stamp.
blocks.summary: Three till receipts on a counter: mono type, a merchant header, features as line items priced INCL with dotted leaders, a subtotal showing the yearly seat discount, a bold TOTAL, a barcode, and a serial footer. The popular plan takes a rotated red rubber stamp; Tilted lays them down at slight angles.
hardParts: The torn bottom edge is a clip-path polygon, so padding must clear the zigzag or text gets cut
Dotted leaders between item and price need a flexible dotted border, not typed periods
The stamp reads as ink only with mix-blend-multiply on paper — and that blend must be undone on dark
blocks.aiHints: A playful, print-flavored pricing section that works for products with simple per-seat maths. The discount line derives from the plan’s monthly and annual prices. Paper stays paper in dark mode — the receipt darkens, the red stamp stays red. Optional eyebrow, heading, and subheading props render a headline styled in this block’s own art direction.

blocks.name: Payments Table
blocks.description: Transactions with people avatars, status pills, filters, row selection and a bulk export bar.
blocks.summary: The billing workhorse: each row pairs a customer photo with their email, a colored status pill, method, date and a tabular-figure amount. Status pills in the toolbar filter the list in place, and selecting rows raises a floating export bar over the table.
hardParts: Selected rows need a static cue — a tint, a rail and a filled checkbox — not just the bulk bar
Amounts only line up when the column switches to tabular figures and end alignment
The bulk bar has to survive a phone width without wrapping to two lines
blocks.aiHints: A transactions or payments list for billing dashboards. Selection is page-scoped; wire bulkActions to your export endpoint. Not a ledger — rows carry no running balance.

blocks.name: Team Members Table
blocks.description: Workspace member management with roles, two-factor status, last activity and a remove action.
blocks.summary: The settings-page staple: member photos with emails, a neutral role badge sorted by rank rather than alphabet, a shielded two-factor indicator, and last-active times. Role pills filter the list, and selection surfaces a destructive remove action in the bulk bar.
hardParts: Roles sort by hierarchy (Owner before Admin before Editor), which needs a rank map, not localeCompare
The 2FA cell pairs a green shield with the word Enabled so state never rides on color alone
Remove is destructive, so it reads in rose inside the bulk bar while staying keyboard reachable
blocks.aiHints: Member management for workspace settings. Wire onSelectedChange and bulkActions to your invite/remove endpoints. Role changes belong in a per-row menu you supply via rowActions.

blocks.name: Invoices Table
blocks.description: Billing history with mono invoice numbers, status pills and a per-row PDF download.
blocks.summary: A quiet billing history: monospaced invoice numbers, billing period, issue date, a paid/due/overdue pill and the amount. Each row reveals a download button on hover that stays reachable by keyboard and visible on touch.
hardParts: Hover-revealed actions must stay in the tab order and visible where hovering does not exist
Overdue needs to read at a glance without turning the whole row red
Invoice numbers are identifiers, so they render in mono and never truncate
blocks.aiHints: A customer-facing billing history. Point the row action at your invoice PDF endpoint. For internal AR work with bulk operations, start from the payments table instead.

blocks.name: Orders Table
blocks.description: E-commerce orders with fulfillment pills, customer avatars and an expandable line-item panel.
blocks.summary: Orders with the detail where you need it: the row shows id, item count, customer, fulfillment state and total, and a disclosure button unfolds the line items — quantity, item and price — on a spring, one order at a time.
hardParts: The line-item panel animates height to auto, which motion has to measure, not guess
Cancelled orders stay neutral — only fulfillment progress earns color
Totals and line prices share one currency formatter so they never disagree
blocks.aiHints: An operations-side order list for e-commerce admin panels. The detail panel renders your line items; swap the fixture for your order shape. Customer-facing order history usually wants the invoices table instead.

blocks.name: Customers Table
blocks.description: Accounts ranked by MRR with plan badges, churn-risk indicators and owner avatars.
blocks.summary: A revenue view for founders: companies with their owner's photo, a plan badge, MRR in tabular figures sorted descending by default, and a churn-risk indicator that pairs a colored dot with the word it means.
hardParts: Churn risk sorts by severity, not alphabetically, which needs a rank map behind the cell
MRR is the default sort — the table must open on the money, not the alphabet
Risk color alone is not state: the dot always carries its label
blocks.aiHints: An account overview for revenue and success teams. Feed it your accounts with mrr as a number; the risk field is a low/medium/high enum you compute upstream.

blocks.name: API Keys Table
blocks.description: Key management with masked secrets in mono, scope chips, usage counts and a revoke action.
blocks.summary: The developer-settings table: key names, secrets masked to dots inside a mono chip, scope chips, last-used times and 30-day call counts. The Revealed variant unmasks every secret at once; the revoke action turns rose on hover.
hardParts: Masking is display-only — the search haystack still matches the real prefix, never the secret
A revoke button that reads as danger on hover but stays quiet in the resting row
Secrets live in a mono chip so a key never breaks across two lines
blocks.aiHints: A key-management section for developer settings. Wire rowActions to your revoke mutation and gate the Revealed state behind a click-to-reveal in production — the variant here is for the specimen.

blocks.name: Audit Log Table
blocks.description: A dense, pinned-header event log with actors, mono action names, IPs and severity levels.
blocks.summary: The enterprise checkbox: 28 events at compact density under a pinned header that picks up a shadow the moment the body scrolls. Actors mix people and service bots, actions render in mono, and severity pairs a dot with its word. The Paged variant trades the scroll box for pagination.
hardParts: A pinned header must be opaque in both themes or rows read straight through it
Service accounts have no photo — they get a terminal glyph so the column never jumps
Times, IPs and action names each need their own alignment and face to scan in a dense grid
blocks.aiHints: A compliance-grade activity feed for admin and security screens. Feed it events newest-first; the level enum is info/warn/error. For user-facing history, the deployments or orders tables read friendlier.

blocks.name: Deployments Table
blocks.description: CI deploys with commit messages, mono shas, environment badges, build status and author avatars.
blocks.summary: A deploy feed the way platform dashboards draw it: commit message over a mono sha, a pulsing dot while a build runs, environment and branch badges, duration, and the author's photo tucked against the age column. Environment pills filter production from previews.
hardParts: The building state pulses its dot — and stops pulsing under reduced motion
Commit messages truncate at a fixed measure so one long message cannot stretch the table
Failed is a terminal state in rose; building is progress in amber — the two must never share a hue
blocks.aiHints: A deployment history for internal platform tools. Statuses are ready/building/failed; the pulse is CSS animate-pulse gated by motion-reduce. Link rows to build logs with onRowClick.

blocks.name: Feature Flags Table
blocks.description: Flag management with env chips, rollout meters and a live spring-animated switch per row.
blocks.summary: A working flags panel: each row carries the flag name over its mono key, environment chips, a rollout meter with its percentage, and a real switch whose knob slides on a spring. Toggles hold live React state, so the specimen actually flips.
hardParts: The switch is a real role=switch button with aria-checked, not a styled div
Toggle state lives outside the column defs, which therefore rebuild through useMemo on change
The rollout meter pairs the bar with a number so the value survives without the visual
blocks.aiHints: An internal flags console. Replace the useState with your flags SDK mutation; the switch is controlled and the table re-renders per toggle. Rollout is display-only here.

blocks.name: Support Tickets Table
blocks.description: A support queue with priority icons, SLA countdowns, assignee avatars and status pills.
blocks.summary: A queue sorted by what burns first: urgent and high priorities carry a warning glyph, the SLA column turns rose when a breach approaches, and each ticket shows requester, assignee photo and a status pill. Status pills filter the queue; default sort is priority, not recency.
hardParts: Priority sorts by severity rank while displaying as words with icons
A breaching SLA needs weight and color together — a red you can also read
Requester context tucks under the subject so the row stays one scan line
blocks.aiHints: A support-team queue for help desks. SLA strings are precomputed upstream; the breaching boolean drives the emphasis. Wire onRowClick to open the ticket.

blocks.name: Top Pages Table
blocks.description: An analytics table with mono paths, share-of-traffic bars and signed week-over-week deltas.
blocks.summary: The table every analytics dashboard ends with: paths in mono, visitor counts scaled against the leader as inline bars, and signed deltas with direction chevrons in green and rose. The Plain variant drops the bars for pure figures.
hardParts: Bars scale against the maximum, floored so the smallest page still shows ink
Deltas need the sign, the chevron and the color to agree at a glance
The minimal surface lets the table sit inside an existing dashboard card
blocks.aiHints: A top-content widget for analytics dashboards. Feed rows sorted or let the default visitors sort handle it. The bar is share-of-leader, not share-of-total — swap the divisor if you need the latter.

blocks.name: Market Watchlist Table
blocks.description: A price watchlist with ticker tiles, signed 24h changes and seven-day inline sparklines.
blocks.summary: A finance surface in five columns: a dark ticker tile, price in tabular figures, a signed 24-hour change with direction chevron, a seven-day sparkline stroked green or rose by trend, and market cap. Minimal surface, built to sit on a dashboard.
hardParts: Sparklines normalize each row against its own range, or flat assets read as cliffs
Gain and loss color must agree across the change cell and the sparkline stroke
Prices keep two decimals in tabular figures so columns of digits align
blocks.aiHints: A watchlist for fintech and crypto dashboards. Trend arrays are the last seven closes; sparklines are plain SVG polylines with no dependencies. For CJK locales, remap gain/loss colors before shipping.

blocks.name: Inventory Table
blocks.description: Stock management with SKU tiles, capacity meters that change color at thresholds and status labels.
blocks.summary: A back-office stock view: product tiles with mono SKUs, a capacity meter that shifts from green through amber to rose as stock thins, the unit count beside it, and a written status so the color never stands alone. Opens sorted by what is running out.
hardParts: Threshold colors derive from stock over capacity, computed in one place for meter and label
Default sort is ascending stock — the emergencies float to the top
Out of stock keeps its meter at zero width instead of hiding it, so columns stay aligned
blocks.aiHints: A stock screen for commerce back offices. Thresholds are 0 and 20% of capacity; adjust stockState for your reorder points. Pair with the orders table for the demand side.

blocks.name: Leaderboard Table
blocks.description: Rankings with medal chips for the top three, player avatars, streaks and weekly movement.
blocks.summary: A leaderboard that celebrates without shouting: gold, silver and bronze chips for the podium, player photos with handles, scores in tabular figures, star-marked streaks, and weekly movement as signed chevrons. Sits on an elevated panel surface.
hardParts: Only the top three earn color — from rank four down, the number is just a number
Movement of zero renders a dash, not a green zero
Rank, score and movement all sort numerically, never as strings
blocks.aiHints: A rankings section for community, gaming or sales dashboards. Ranks come precomputed in the data; the table sorts by them rather than deriving order. Streak and movement are optional columns to delete.

blocks.name: Files Table
blocks.description: A shared-drive browser with type-glyph tiles, sizes, collaborator stacks and modified dates.
blocks.summary: A file browser in table form: folder, document, image and video glyphs in soft tiles, a name over its format line, human-readable sizes, an overlapping stack of collaborator photos, and modified dates. Folders sort with a dash for size instead of a fake number.
hardParts: Four Iconly file-type glyphs pick by kind through one lookup, not a chain of ternaries
The avatar stack overlaps with surface-colored rings so it works on white and near-black
Folder sizes are null — they sort to the bottom and print as a dash, never 0 KB
blocks.aiHints: A drive or attachments browser for productivity tools. Kind is a folder/doc/image/video enum that picks the glyph; extend the map for more types. Wire onRowClick to open entries.

blocks.name: Market Chart
blocks.description: A trading-desk chart in pure SVG: OHLC candles, a volume pane, a snapping crosshair and a live tape.
blocks.summary: The full trading surface, drawn without a charting library: candles over a volume pane, a crosshair that pins price and time to both axes, a range selector that morphs the series, and an optional live tape. Arrow keys scrub it once the plot has focus.
hardParts: Candles need { t, open, high, low, close, volume } with t in epoch milliseconds
live appends simulated ticks — drive it from your own socket by feeding data instead
Scrubbing blocks only the axis it scrubs on, so a drag never traps page scroll on touch
blocks.aiHints: A full trading surface for a market page. Dependency-free SVG. Use Candlestick Chart if you only need candles inside an existing Recharts layout.
notes: Candles need `{ t, open, high, low, close, volume }` with `t` in epoch milliseconds.
`live` appends simulated ticks — drive it from your own socket by feeding `data` instead.
Arrow keys scrub the crosshair once the plot has focus.

blocks.name: Candlestick Chart
blocks.description: OHLC candles with optional volume and hollow-up bodies, for stocks and any market pair.
blocks.summary: Candles that drop into an existing Recharts layout, with a volume pane and hollow bodies for up sessions. For a full trading surface with a crosshair and a range selector, reach for the Market Chart instead.
hardParts: Built on Recharts — for a full trading surface use the Market Chart instead
Up and down carry an outline as well as a colour, so direction survives colour-blindness
Volume shares the candle scale band rather than a second axis
blocks.aiHints: Candles inside a Recharts page. Needs OHLC rows; showVolume adds the pane. Market Chart is the dependency-free alternative.
notes: Built on Recharts. For a full trading surface use the Market Chart instead.

blocks.name: Price Chart
blocks.description: Ticker chrome with last price and signed delta — for tokens, equities or protocol TVL.
blocks.summary: A price line under a header that carries the symbol, the last print and the signed change. The Compare variant indexes two series to a common base so their shapes can be read against each other on one axis.
hardParts: Comparing two instruments means indexing both to 100 at t0 — never a second Y axis
The delta colours by direction and repeats the sign, so it is not colour alone
Last price sits in tabular figures, or the header jitters on every tick
blocks.aiHints: A ticker panel for a token, equity or TVL series. Compare takes two series indexed to a shared base.
notes: Compare indexes both series to a common base — two Y axes would invent a correlation.

blocks.name: Indicator Chart
blocks.description: Price, RSI and MACD stacked on one time axis with a single crosshair across all three panes.
blocks.summary: Three panes that share one time axis and one crosshair, so a reading in the price pane lines up with its RSI and MACD values. Both indicators are computed from the full series and then sliced, so changing range never restates them.
hardParts: RSI and MACD are computed from the full series, then sliced — restating them per range would move history
rsi() and macd() are exported if you want the numbers without the chart
One crosshair drives three panes, so the hover index lives above them, not inside each
blocks.aiHints: Technical analysis view for a trading page. Takes the same candles as Market Chart; indicators are derived, not passed.
notes: RSI and MACD are computed from the full series, then sliced — so changing range never restates them.
`rsi()` and `macd()` are exported if you want the numbers without the chart.

blocks.name: Depth Chart
blocks.description: Cumulative bid and ask liquidity either side of the mid, with a crosshair that reports resting size.
blocks.summary: The liquidity curve either side of the mid price, with a crosshair that reports how much size rests up to any price. Levels are cumulative outward from the mid, so the slope is the cost of sweeping the book.
hardParts: generateOrderBook() from the engine builds a specimen book; swap it for your feed
Levels are cumulative from the mid outward — pass total already summed
Bid and ask are the up and down tokens, repeated as left and right of the mid
blocks.aiHints: Liquidity depth for a DEX or exchange page. Takes a book with cumulative bid and ask levels; pair it with the Order Book ladder.
notes: `generateOrderBook()` from the engine builds a specimen book; swap it for your feed.
Levels are cumulative from the mid outward — pass `total` already summed.

blocks.name: Order Book
blocks.description: A trading ladder with cumulative depth bars, a spread row and flashing updates in live mode.
blocks.summary: The bid and ask ladder with depth bars behind the rows and a spread row between the sides. Hovering a row highlights every level between it and the touch — the cost of sweeping to that price.
hardParts: Hovering a row highlights every level between it and the touch — the sweep cost, not just the row
live re-derives the book from a seeded nonce, so it stays deterministic across renders
Prices and sizes are tabular, or the ladder shivers on every update
blocks.aiHints: The bid/ask ladder beside a trading chart. Deterministic under live mode, so it is safe to server-render.
notes: Hovering a row highlights every level between it and the touch — the sweep cost.
`live` re-derives the book from a seeded nonce, so it stays deterministic across renders.

blocks.name: Portfolio Chart
blocks.description: Account value against cost basis, with drawdown from the running peak shaded underneath.
blocks.summary: Account value over capital deployed, with the drawdown from the running peak shaded below the line. The stepped dashed line is the basis, so gains read as the gap between the two.
hardParts: Drawdown is measured from the running peak inside the visible range, not all time
basis is capital deployed to date — the stepped dashed line, not a smooth series
Profit and loss share one axis; the shading carries the second reading instead
blocks.aiHints: Portfolio value with cost basis and drawdown. points need value and basis; drawdown is derived.
notes: Drawdown is measured from the running peak inside the visible range, not all time.
`basis` is capital deployed to date — the stepped dashed line.

blocks.name: Area Chart
blocks.description: Filled areas with gradient, hatch, dotted, stacked and dashed-stroke variants.
blocks.summary: The workhorse trend chart, with seven fills that change the character of the plot without touching the data. Axes, grid and tooltip are real Recharts children, so the chart keeps its ticks when you restyle it.
hardParts: Axes and grids are direct Recharts children — wrap one in a component and Recharts silently drops it
Stacked areas need the series order fixed, or the bands reshuffle between renders
The animated dashed stroke runs on a keyframe that stops under reduced motion
blocks.aiHints: Trends over time where volume matters. variant switches the fill; stackType stacks series. Use Price Chart for a ticker with chrome.
notes: Built on Recharts. Axes, grid and tooltip must stay direct children — a wrapper component is dropped silently.

blocks.name: Bar Chart
blocks.description: Vertical and horizontal bars with hatch, duotone, gradient, stripe, stack, percent and glow fills.
blocks.summary: Ten presentations of the same bar chart, from a plain column to a 100% stack and a horizontal ranking. Every variant keeps real axes and gridlines, and the percent stack computes its own shares.
hardParts: Horizontal bars need the category on the Y axis and a wider left margin, or labels clip
The percent variant normalises to 100 itself — pass raw values, not shares
Duotone reverse swaps which half of the stack carries the accent, so the eye reads the remainder
blocks.aiHints: Comparing categories or stacked composition. variant picks the fill; layout="vertical" gives horizontal bars. Cap categorical series at six.
notes: Built on Recharts. Axes, grid and tooltip must stay direct children — a wrapper component is dropped silently.

blocks.name: Line Chart
blocks.description: Multi-series lines with solid, dashed, bump, step, gradient and glow strokes.
blocks.summary: Multi-series lines with six stroke treatments and a shared tooltip. Step is for values that hold between readings, bump for smooth interpolation, and the gradient stroke fades a series toward the axis.
hardParts: curveType changes meaning, not just shape — step says the value held, bump says it moved smoothly
A dashed stroke reads as projection or forecast, so do not use it for actuals
Legends carry identity for every series past the first, so lines are never distinguished by colour alone
blocks.aiHints: Trends where the reader compares series. curveType switches interpolation; keep to four series or facet into small multiples.
notes: Built on Recharts. Axes, grid and tooltip must stay direct children — a wrapper component is dropped silently.

blocks.name: Composed Chart
blocks.description: Bars, lines and areas on one plot — mix fills, dashes and glow per series.
blocks.summary: One plot carrying more than one mark type: bars for the measure, a line for the trend or target, an area for the band behind them. All of it on a single shared axis.
hardParts: Every series shares one Y axis — a second scale would invent a correlation that is not in the data
Mark type is the strongest channel, so give the bars the measure people came to read
Series order controls paint order; the line has to come after the bars or it hides behind them
blocks.aiHints: One plot mixing marks — bars with a trend line, or an area with a target. Keep both measures on one scale.
notes: Built on Recharts. Never add a second Y axis — index both measures to a common base instead.

blocks.name: Pie Chart
blocks.description: Pie and donut charts with padded sectors, labels and optional sector glow.
blocks.summary: Part-to-whole at a glance, with a donut that can carry a total in its middle and padded sectors that separate on the surface rather than with a stroke. Labels ride the sectors only when they fit.
hardParts: Six segments is the ceiling — past that, fold the tail into one Other slice
Padded sectors separate with surface, not a border, so the ring keeps its weight
A pie cannot rank close values; switch to bars when the reader needs an order
blocks.aiHints: Composition at a glance for six or fewer segments. Donut variant frees the middle for a total. Not for ranking.
notes: Part-to-whole only, and never for comparing close values — use a bar chart there.

blocks.name: Radar Chart
blocks.description: Radar plots with filled or outline series, circle grids and glow.
blocks.summary: A profile across several axes at once — scorecards, feature coverage, skill maps. Filled for one series, outlines when two profiles are being compared.
hardParts: Every axis has to share a scale, or the shape is decorative rather than readable
Two filled series obscure each other; use the Lines variant to compare
Axis order changes the silhouette, so fix it once and keep it across screens
blocks.aiHints: Multi-attribute profiles on one shared scale. Two series maximum; normalise attributes before passing them.
notes: Every axis must share one scale, or the polygon means nothing.

blocks.name: Radial Chart
blocks.description: Full and semi-circle radial bars for share and progress.
blocks.summary: Progress toward a target as an arc, with a full circle for share and a semi-circle for a gauge that sits above a caption. The track is a lighter step of the fill, so state reads across the whole arc.
hardParts: The track is a lighter step of the fill hue, so the unfilled remainder still reads as the same measure
Arc length is hard to compare across cards — label the number, always
A semi-circle needs its own vertical rhythm or the caption floats away from the arc
blocks.aiHints: Single-value progress or share. One or two arcs per card; use bars when comparing more than three values.
notes: Always print the number: arc length is the weakest comparison channel there is.

blocks.name: Histogram
blocks.description: Raw samples binned on nice edges, with the long tail folded into one labelled overflow bin.
blocks.summary: The chart that shows the tail an average hides. It bins raw samples itself on human-readable edges, pins p50, p95 and p99 onto the plot, and folds everything past the 99th percentile into a single overflow bin past a broken axis — so a distribution with one 900ms straggler still fills the plot instead of spending half of it on air.
hardParts: Pass raw samples — the chart bins them itself on human-readable edges rather than trusting yours
The tail folds into one overflow bin past a visible axis break, so clipping it never reads as missing data
Percentiles ride one hue that darkens with k; red on p99 would call the tail bad, which is not the chart’s call
blocks.aiHints: Latency, order value or any distribution where the tail matters. Feed raw samples, not pre-bucketed counts; tailCutoff controls the overflow bin. Not a time series.
notes: Pass raw samples — the chart bins them itself on human-readable edges.
`tailCutoff` is the percentile past which samples fold into the overflow bin; pass `100` to bin the full range.
`buildBins()`, `percentile()` and `splitTail()` are exported if you need the numbers elsewhere.

blocks.name: Connecting Real Data
blocks.description: Wiring any chart to a real source: fetch, SWR or React Query, server components and streaming.
blocks.summary: Three recipes for getting real data into a chart, with every outcome mapped onto the same status union the charts already take. One hook drives all of them, and its retry wires straight into the error state.
hardParts: Every chart takes the same status union, so one fetch hook drives all of them
retry is wired to the error state’s button — pass it straight through as onRetry
Streaming appends to the series instead of replacing it, so the chart animates rather than jumps
blocks.aiHints: How to feed the charts from an API. useChartData returns { data, status, retry } shaped for the ChartState contract.
notes: Every chart takes the same `status` union, so one fetch hook drives all of them.
`retry` is wired to the error state’s button — pass it straight through as `onRetry`.

blocks.name: Stat Cards
blocks.description: KPI cards with a big value, the delta written as a sentence, and a scrubbable sparkline beside it.
blocks.summary: The row every dashboard opens with. Each card carries a label, a compact value, the change written out against a named period, and either a scrubbable sparkline or a progress bar. Hovering the spark reports the point under the pointer instead of the headline figure.
hardParts: Set goodWhen: 'down' on metrics where falling is healthy, like churn, or the delta turns red on good news
Pass previous to compare against last period rather than the first point in the series
A card with progress renders a bar instead of a sparkline, so the row can mix both shapes
blocks.aiHints: The KPI header for an analytics dashboard. Cards are data, not markup — pass value, previous, series and goodWhen. Not a chart panel: one metric per card.
notes: Set `goodWhen: 'down'` on metrics where falling is healthy, like churn — otherwise the delta turns red.
Pass `previous` to compare against last period instead of the first point in the series.
A card with `progress` renders a bar instead of a sparkline.

blocks.name: Cohort Retention
blocks.description: The retention triangle: cohorts down, periods across, intensity by share retained.
blocks.summary: A cohort grid with a row and column crosshair and a period average underneath. Later cohorts carry shorter arrays, so the ragged edge stays honest about which periods have actually happened.
hardParts: Give later cohorts shorter retention arrays — the ragged edge is the point, not a gap to fill with zeros
Index 0 should always be 100; the chart does not normalise for you
Intensity runs on one hue, so darkness reads as magnitude rather than as a second category
blocks.aiHints: Retention by signup cohort for growth dashboards. data is an array of cohorts with a label, size and retention array; period labels the columns.
notes: Give later cohorts shorter `retention` arrays — the ragged edge is the point.
Index 0 should always be 100; the chart does not normalise for you.

blocks.name: Calendar Heatmap
blocks.description: A year of daily values as week columns — the contributions grid, with streak stats and month rails.
blocks.summary: Five quantised intensity steps across a year of week columns, with month rails above and streak and busiest-day figures beside it. Gaps in the data fill as zero, so a sparse feed still renders a complete year.
hardParts: Days need { t, value } with t at UTC midnight; gaps are filled as zero rather than skipped
Intensity is quantised into five buckets — the eye cannot rank a continuous ramp
Month labels print on the column each month starts, not on every column
blocks.aiHints: Daily activity density — commits, deploys, orders, sessions. Expects a full year of { t, value }; use the Cohort chart for retention grids instead.
notes: Days need `{ t, value }` with `t` at UTC midnight; gaps are filled as zero.
Intensity is quantised into five buckets — the eye cannot rank a continuous ramp.

blocks.name: Mega Sitemap Footer
blocks.description: A 54-link enterprise sitemap with stacked sub-groups, a newsletter block and a locale bar.
blocks.summary: The footer an enterprise site actually ships: five ruled columns each stacking two sub-groups, fifty-four links, per-group 'see all' links, a newsletter block beside the brand, and a bottom bar carrying mono-caps legal, social glyphs and region and language pills. Below lg every sub-group becomes an accordion.
hardParts: Density is the design — twenty links reads as a placeholder, so columns stack sub-groups the way Razorpay, GitHub and Stripe do rather than padding one list each
A per-column top rule beats a full-width one: it survives columns of wildly different height without leaving a rule floating over whitespace
The legal list wraps and the locale controls do not, or the language pill drops to its own line the moment a company name gets long

The five columns resolve left to right on a view() timeline as the footer scrolls in, and cannot strand a link mid-fade: for anything at the end of a document the entry range is guaranteed to reach 100% at maximum scroll
blocks.aiHints: Reach for this when a large B2B site needs its whole information architecture in the footer. Presentational — pass groups, legal links and the region and language option lists. It does not persist the selection or route on change; wire onChange yourself via the native select.

blocks.name: Trust Center Footer
blocks.description: Compliance badges that expand on hover, over a customer logo row and link columns.
blocks.summary: The footer a procurement team reads. Five certifications expand to scope and report date on hover or focus, a row of customer logos says who already runs it, and four link columns keep it a footer rather than a banner.
hardParts: A badge is worth nothing without scope and a date — the reveal exists so the card can carry both without shouting them
Hover-only disclosure strands keyboard users, so focus and blur drive the same state as pointer enter and leave
The Detailed variant renders every card open, because print and reduced-interaction contexts get no hover at all
The logo row is a grid rather than a wrapping flex row: six names of uneven length left a single orphan on the second line at most widths
blocks.aiHints: Use on regulated B2B marketing sites where the footer is the first thing a security reviewer scans. Data in, callback out — badges are an array with scope, issue date and href. It renders no certification imagery; supply your own logos if you have the licences.

blocks.name: Region Picker Footer
blocks.description: A region popover with locale, currency, data residency and live local time.
blocks.summary: Multi-region products owe the reader a residency answer in the footer. This one lists regions with their locale, currency and cloud region, and ticks a live local clock beside each so a reader in Osaka can see who is awake.
hardParts: The clock renders as dashes on the server and fills in after mount — a real time on first paint is a hydration mismatch
The popover closes on outside pointerdown and on Escape, and cleans both listeners up when it closes
The check mark cross-fades on scale and blur rather than appearing, so switching regions does not flicker
blocks.aiHints: Reach for this when a product has genuine data-residency choices to state. Controlled or uncontrolled — pass value plus onChange, or let it hold its own. Optional groups render link columns above the utility row. It does not route, set a cookie, or migrate anything; the copy says so, and you should keep that line.

blocks.name: Service Status Footer
blocks.description: Thirty days of per-service uptime bars with a rolling incident ticker.
blocks.summary: Statuspage, shrunk to footer height. Each service gets thirty days of uptime as one bar per day graded by colour, a live summary pill that reports the worst service, and an incident ticker that rolls every few seconds.
hardParts: Uptime lives between 0.98 and 1.00, so mapping it to bar height draws thirty near-identical stubs and reads as noise — the signal has to be colour, with the bars a constant height
The summary pill reports the worst service, not the first, or a single outage hides behind four green rows
Bars are flex-1 with a floor rather than a fixed width, so thirty days fill whatever width the card has
blocks.aiHints: Use when uptime is part of the sales argument and the status page deserves a permanent footer slot. Purely presentational: history is an array of 0–1 ratios oldest to newest. It does not poll — feed it from your own status API on the server.

blocks.name: Sales CTA Footer
blocks.description: A seat slider that prices a tier live, beside the link grid.
blocks.summary: Enterprise pricing is quoted, not listed, which leaves prospects guessing. This footer lets them move a seat slider and watch a tier and an indicative annual figure resolve, then hands them a contact button that knows the number they picked.
hardParts: Both readouts are tabular-nums; proportional figures wobble the layout on every step of the drag
The filled track is a separate absolutely positioned span so the range input keeps its native keyboard behaviour
The estimate is labelled indicative in the block itself — a footer calculator that reads as a quote is a support ticket
blocks.aiHints: Reach for this on a per-seat B2B product whose real price is negotiated. onContact receives the current seat count so the lead arrives pre-qualified. Tier thresholds and discounts are hard-coded in the file — edit TIERS to match your rate card.

blocks.name: Link Search Footer
blocks.description: Type-to-filter across every footer link, with arrow-key navigation.
blocks.summary: Past about forty links a footer stops being navigation and becomes a wall. This one puts a combobox in front of the wall: type and the columns are replaced by ranked matches with the hit highlighted and the section named, arrow keys move the cursor, Escape restores the grid.
hardParts: The full grid stays in the DOM until a query exists, so crawlers and no-JS readers still see every link
Matching runs over the label and the section title, so typing a section name surfaces its pages
Highlighting slices the label around the match rather than using dangerouslySetInnerHTML on user input
blocks.aiHints: Use on documentation-heavy or multi-product sites whose footer link count has outgrown scanning. Client-side filter over the groups you pass — no index, no fetch. Results cap at seven; raise the slice if your sections are broader.

blocks.name: Careers Footer
blocks.description: A rolling three-role window with department filters, over link columns.
blocks.summary: Hiring, without turning the footer into a job board. Department chips filter the list, three roles are visible at a time and the window rolls one row every few seconds, and four link columns sit underneath so the block still reads as a footer.
hardParts: A one-role ticker leaves a tall card that is mostly empty — three rows rolling one at a time keeps the motion and fills the space
Rows are keyed on the window offset as well as the role, so only the row that actually changed replays its entrance
Filtering resets the window, or switching department leaves the ticker pointing past the end of a shorter list
blocks.aiHints: Reach for this when open roles are worth surfacing on every page. Data in, no fetching — pass roles with title, department, location and type. The ticker pauses for nobody; set variant to List when the full set matters more than the motion.

blocks.name: Policy Footer
blocks.description: Cookie-category switches with a save state, over a layered legal row.
blocks.summary: The legal floor of a multi-entity company: registered names, a cookie preferences panel with per-category switches, and a policy row covering DPA, sub-processors and accessibility. Strictly necessary is locked on and says so.
hardParts: The locked category renders as a disabled switch with an Always on marker instead of vanishing, so the list stays honest
Saved is announced through aria-live and fades rather than appearing, so a screen reader hears the result of the click
The switch knob transitions on left rather than transform, which keeps it crisp against the 22px track at any zoom
blocks.aiHints: Use where consent management has to be reachable from every page. onSave receives the enabled category ids; it stores nothing itself, so connect it to your CMP. Not a substitute for a consent banner on first visit.

blocks.name: Model Status Footer
blocks.description: A model availability grid with animated latency bars and context sizes.
blocks.summary: What an inference platform owes its users at the bottom of every page: which models are up, how fast they are answering, and how much context they take. Latency bars are drawn relative to the slowest model in the set, so the comparison is honest.
hardParts: Bars scale against the slowest model rather than a fixed ceiling, so adding a slow model rescales the whole set correctly
The operational ping is a second absolutely positioned dot; animating the dot itself would move the status indicator
Latency and context are tabular-nums in a fixed-width column, so the rows stay aligned as numbers change
blocks.aiHints: Reach for this on an LLM API or inference product where model health is the headline. Presentational — pass models with latency in milliseconds and a health state. It does not poll a status endpoint; render it from server data.

blocks.name: Command Footer
blocks.description: A terminal footer with slash commands, inline completion and Tab to accept.
blocks.summary: Navigation as a prompt. Type a slash command and the rest of it appears in ghost text behind the caret, Tab accepts, Enter runs, arrow keys move through the list, and run commands stack above as history.
hardParts: The ghost completion is a second absolutely positioned span with the typed prefix rendered invisible, so it tracks the caret at any width
Tab is intercepted only when a completion exists, so the footer never traps keyboard focus
The blinking caret is steps(1,end), not a fade — a fading terminal caret reads as a bug
blocks.aiHints: Use for developer-facing AI and infrastructure products whose audience lives in a shell. onRun receives the command string; routing is yours. Commands are a static array — it does not fuzzy-match or execute anything.

blocks.name: Ask Docs Footer
blocks.description: A question input that streams a cited answer in place.
blocks.summary: The footer as a retrieval surface. Ask a question and the panel opens with a searching state, then streams the answer character by character and settles into a row of numbered citation chips.
hardParts: Three phases — thinking, streaming, done — because a caret that starts before the first token pretends latency does not exist
Citations appear only once streaming finishes, so the layout does not reflow under the reader mid-sentence
The streaming caret is inline and baseline-shifted, so it sits on the text rather than floating above the descenders
blocks.aiHints: Reach for this when documentation search is the main thing readers want from the footer. The answer prop is the text it streams — swap the canned string for your own retrieval result. It performs no fetching and holds no conversation history.

blocks.name: Wordmark Spotlight Footer
blocks.description: A full-bleed wordmark lit by a spotlight that follows the pointer.
blocks.summary: The big-footer masthead, done without a canvas. A near-invisible wordmark spans the page, and a second copy at full brightness is revealed through a radial mask that tracks the pointer.
hardParts: Two stacked copies with a CSS mask beats any per-letter approach — the light crosses letterforms instead of switching them
The visible text is aria-hidden twice over with one screen-reader-only copy, so the wordmark is announced once, not three times
Font size is a clamp against viewport width, so the wordmark stays edge-to-edge from phone to ultrawide without a resize listener
blocks.aiHints: Use where the brand is the point and the footer is the last impression — AI labs, studios, design-led products. Pointer only by design; there is nothing to reveal on touch, and the Static variant is the honest fallback.

blocks.name: Token Stream Footer
blocks.description: A manifesto that types itself in word by word when the footer enters view.
blocks.summary: A closing statement that arrives the way the product's own output does. An IntersectionObserver starts the stream when the footer reaches the viewport, and each word fades up out of a blur, over a row of platform figures.
hardParts: The full sentence is on the paragraph's aria-label, so assistive tech reads it whole rather than word by word as it lands
Unlanded words render invisible rather than unmounted, so the paragraph is full height from the first frame and nothing below it reflows mid-stream
Reduced motion is checked before the observer is even attached, and settles the sentence complete instead of streaming it
blocks.aiHints: Reach for this on an AI product landing page where the footer carries a positioning statement. Keep the manifesto under about thirty words; past that the stream outlasts the reader's patience. Purely visual — no data, no callbacks.

blocks.name: Neural Grid Footer
blocks.description: An SVG node lattice that lights up under the pointer.
blocks.summary: Generative texture without a canvas or a render loop. A deterministic SVG lattice of nodes and short edges sits behind the links, and a bright duplicate is revealed through a pointer-tracked mask with its edges flowing.
hardParts: Node jitter comes from a seeded sine, not Math.random, so the server and client draw the same lattice and hydration holds
Nodes live in normalised 0–1 space and a ResizeObserver feeds the viewBox the container's real aspect — a fixed viewBox stretches every circle into an ellipse
The pointer handler writes the mask straight to the DOM inside a rAF, so moving the mouse never re-renders React
blocks.aiHints: Use where an AI product wants atmosphere in the footer without shipping a WebGL dependency. Decorative and aria-hidden throughout. Edge count grows quadratically with node count — keep the arrays near the defaults.

blocks.name: Release Feed Footer
blocks.description: A model and API changelog on a dated rail, with kind chips.
blocks.summary: Fast-moving AI products ship weekly and bury it in a changelog nobody opens. This footer puts the last five releases on a dated rail with a chip marking model, API or platform, and the hovered entry lights its node.
hardParts: Dates are in a fixed-width gutter outside the rail, so the timeline stays a straight line whatever the date format
The rail nodes carry a ring in the surface colour, which is what makes them read as sitting on the line rather than behind it
Hover and focus set the same active entry, so the rail highlight follows keyboard tabbing as well as the pointer
blocks.aiHints: Reach for this when release cadence is itself a selling point. Pass releases newest first with a pre-formatted date string — it does no date parsing or locale formatting. Kind maps to three tones; add your own in KIND_TONE.

blocks.name: API Playground Footer
blocks.description: A copyable curl or Python snippet with an endpoint switcher and token count.
blocks.summary: The shortest path from footer to first API call. Endpoint tabs swap the snippet, the language variant swaps curl for the SDK, a copy button cross-fades to a tick, and the status strip reports the runtime and the input token count.
hardParts: Copy feedback cross-fades two icons that both stay mounted, so the exit animates instead of the tick popping in
The pre is keyed on endpoint and language so the snippet animates on switch rather than silently swapping text
Right padding on the pre reserves the copy button's column, so long lines scroll under it instead of behind it
blocks.aiHints: Use on developer-first AI and API products where the footer should convert a reader into a caller. Snippets are strings you supply — it does not highlight syntax or run anything. Pair with the Shiki-rendered code block if you need colour.

blocks.name: Newsletter Footer
blocks.description: A newsletter capture with inline validation and a success morph.
blocks.summary: The conversion footer for a small product. A large capture panel states the cadence and the list size honestly, validates on submit, shakes once on a bad address, and morphs the whole field into a confirmation that quotes the address back.
hardParts: The helper line holds its slot in both states, so the error message does not push the link grid down the page
aria-invalid and aria-describedby wire the error to the input, so it is announced rather than only shown
The shake is 320ms and runs once — a looping error animation reads as a broken form
blocks.aiHints: Reach for this when the footer's job is list growth. onSubscribe receives the validated address; the block never posts anywhere. Validation is a shape check, not a deliverability check — verify server-side.

blocks.name: Contact Card Footer
blocks.description: Copyable email, phone and address rows with opening hours and local time.
blocks.summary: For teams small enough that contact is a person, not a portal. Each row is both a link and a copy target, the copy button appears on hover and on focus, and a live local clock next to the opening hours says whether anyone is actually there.
hardParts: Every row is a link and a copy button — one hit target for each, never overlapping, both keyboard reachable
The clock only renders after mount, because a server-rendered time is a hydration mismatch waiting to happen
The copy button reveals on group hover but is always visible on focus, otherwise it is unreachable by keyboard
blocks.aiHints: Use for agencies, studios and small SaaS where the footer replaces a contact page. utcOffset is a plain hour offset and does not handle daylight saving — pass the current offset, or drop the prop to hide the clock.

blocks.name: Logo Wall Footer
blocks.description: A customer logo wall — scrolling marquee or plotted grid — over a rating row and stats that count up.
blocks.summary: The "trusted by" block, done properly. Twelve customer marks run as an edge-masked marquee that pauses under the pointer, or settle into a plotted grid whose cells stagger in. Under them a rating row and four counters that animate once when the footer enters view.
hardParts: A seamless marquee is the list twice over and a keyframe that travels exactly -50%, so the seam lands where the second copy sits pixel-for-pixel on the first
The edge mask is what makes it read as a wall rather than a widget — without it logos are chopped by the viewport edge instead of dissolving
Logos ship as inlined geometry on a 24px grid rather than image files, so they take theme colour, stay crisp at any size, and add no network requests
Counters run once on intersection and are skipped entirely under reduced motion, where the final figure is what renders
blocks.aiHints: Reach for this when a footer needs social proof. Pass `customers` as name plus an SVG component; the bundled set is invented, so replace it with real marks before shipping. Stats are presentational — the count-up is animation only, not live data.

blocks.name: Minimal Footer
blocks.description: A single-line footer whose link clusters expand on hover or focus.
blocks.summary: Everything a small site needs in one 30px row. Section names sit as quiet buttons; hovering or focusing one lifts a small panel of its links above the bar, so the footer stays one line without losing a page.
hardParts: Panels open upward, because a footer popover that opens downward opens off the bottom of the document
Hover opens and focus opens, and pointer-leaving the whole footer closes — otherwise a panel is left hanging
Buttons carry aria-expanded, so the disclosure is announced rather than being pure hover decoration
blocks.aiHints: Use on personal sites, docs and small products where a five-column footer would be theatre. Links live inside the panels, so if crawlability of every footer link matters more than the single line, take the mega sitemap instead.

blocks.name: Big Type Footer
blocks.description: An oversized wordmark, justified edge to edge, whose letters lift on hover.
blocks.summary: The editorial masthead footer. The brand name is split into letters spread across the full width, each lifting slightly under the pointer, over a compact set of columns and a call to action.
hardParts: Per-letter font size is derived from the letter count, so a four-letter and a twelve-letter brand both fill the width

A mount-time entrance on a footer plays to an empty room, so the letters hang off a view() scroll timeline and stagger by shifting each one’s animation-range — animation-delay does nothing on a scroll timeline
The word is on an aria-label with every letter aria-hidden, otherwise a screen reader spells the brand out

The root has to be overflow-clip rather than overflow-hidden: hidden makes the footer its own scroll container, which is what the letters’ timeline would then measure against, freezing every one of them
blocks.aiHints: Reach for this when the brand should be the last thing on the page. Best for wordmarks of four to twelve characters; longer names shrink past the point where the effect reads. Purely typographic — no image assets. The scroll-driven reveal is progressive enhancement — browsers without animation-timeline, and anyone on reduced motion, get the resting state.

blocks.name: Parallax Reveal Footer
blocks.description: A footer pinned behind the page that the content slides up to reveal.
blocks.summary: The reveal footer, in about fifteen lines of CSS and no scroll listener. The footer is sticky to the bottom of the scroll container from the start; the page above it carries an opaque background and a lifted shadow, so scrolling uncovers rather than moves.
hardParts: Sticky beats a scroll listener outright — the browser owns the pin, so there is no jank and no rAF budget spent
The reveal only exists if the content above is opaque and stacked over the footer; a transparent page shows both at once
It takes the page content as children rather than assuming a page structure, so it works inside a panel as well as a document
blocks.aiHints: Use at the bottom of a long marketing page for a closing beat. Pass the scrolling content as children; without children it renders flat, which is also the correct reduced-motion fallback. Needs a scroll container — page or a sized div.

blocks.name: Marquee CTA Footer
blocks.description: An infinite CTA band that pauses on hover, over a compact link row.
blocks.summary: A closing band that keeps moving until the reader points at it. Short phrases scroll in a seamless loop across a full-width link, separated by dots, with a straight and a tilted ribbon variant.
hardParts: The loop duplicates the phrase list and translates exactly -50%, the only offset that hides the wrap point
The whole band is one anchor, so the moving text is a single hit target instead of a row of moving ones
Pausing on hover uses animation-play-state, which resumes from where it stopped instead of restarting the loop
blocks.aiHints: Reach for this when the footer should carry one loud call to action. Keep phrases to four or five of about four words; a long phrase list slows the perceived loop to a crawl. Speed is seconds per full pass.

blocks.name: Studio Footer
blocks.description: An accent switcher, a now-building ticker and a live studio clock.
blocks.summary: The footer of a product with three people behind it. An accent swatch row recolours the footer live through a CSS variable, a small equaliser sits beside a rotating now-building line, and the copyright row carries the studio's local time.
hardParts: The accent is one CSS custom property on the footer element, so a click recolours every dependent without re-rendering them
Swatches resize rather than gaining a ring, which keeps the selected state legible against any colour including the pale ones
The equaliser bars keep a floor height under reduced motion instead of freezing flat, which would read as broken
blocks.aiHints: Use for indie products, studios and side projects whose footer is allowed a personality. onAccentChange hands back the chosen accent so you can lift it into your own theme; the block only recolours itself.

blocks.name: Waitlist Footer
blocks.description: Waitlist capture with an avatar stack and a live position counter.
blocks.summary: A pre-launch footer that tells the truth about the queue. An email field under an ambient glow, an avatar stack with a running total, and on submit the field becomes the reader's position in line.
hardParts: The submitted state names a position rather than saying thanks, which is the only part of a waitlist a reader wants
The sheen is a skewed span clipped by the button, so it sweeps the fill instead of animating the button itself
Avatars carry an explicit z-index descending by index, so the overlap stacks left over right at any list length
blocks.aiHints: Reach for this before launch, when the footer's only job is the list. onJoin receives the validated address and the count increments locally for feedback only — the real number has to come from your backend.
